newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks bounce back to advance one percent.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks bounce back to advance one percent.

text.p: Swiss blue chips closed more than one percent higher on Thursday as buyers returned to the market after a two-day consolidation, dealers said.
However, the market was cautious and kept an eye on Wall Street to be on the safe side in case the U.S. market started to consolidate recent gains, they said.
Novartis and UBS, under slight pressure earlier this week, led the market higher while Roche rose only a little.
The broad Swiss Performance Index rose 34.07 points to 3,405.95.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index was up 55.6 to 5,364.2.
"The market advanced less than we had expected. That shows that people are cautious," one dealer said, adding that the SMI index met some resistance at 5,360.
ABB lost 22 francs to close at 2,163 on news that Swedish investment group Incentive sold part of its holdings in ABB to Morgan Stanley.
Dealers said some investors took the news on ABB as a reason to take profits.
And there was some uncertainty surrounding the share as long as it was unclear who was going to buy the ABB shares from Morgan Stanley.
Insurers showed slight gains, with Zurich group one franc higher at 559.

Among banks, CS Holding eased 0.75 francs to 191.50 while UBS added 24 to 1,688. Dealers said some speculative investors had been disappointed that CS Group had not announced any major deal yet such as closer cooperation with an insurer.
Trade on Soffex was quiet. Index options made up 51 percent of options trade, dealers said. Futures moved on both sides of the fair-value line on 4,663 contracts.
